en: The Sūtra of the Venerable and Victorious Great Wisdom King,
translated by the Tripitaka Master Śīladharma, Imperially Appointed Court Disperser, Acting Assistant Director of the Court of State Ceremonial,
and Great Master of the Transmission of the Dharma, under Imperial Decree.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed Ānanda, saying:
"Ānanda, there is a most venerable and supreme Great Brightness King (Mahāvidyārāja),
which was proclaimed by all the Buddhas of the past."
Ānanda, those seven koṭis of Tathāgatas also joyfully proclaimed it;
I now, in turn, proclaim and manifest it for the sake of all sentient beings in future ages.
Listen attentively, Ānanda!
If there are sons or daughters of good family who,
having heard this most venerable and supreme vidyā-mantra, wish to receive, uphold, read, and recite it.
First, one must purify body and mind.
One takes refuge in all Buddhas, all Honored Dharmas, and all Noble Sanghas.
Furthermore, one takes refuge in the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara of Great Compassion.
I also take refuge in and beseech the protection of the Lord of the Sahā World,
as well as all the vidyādharas and others.
Having thus taken refuge in these Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and noble assemblies:
Thereafter, one may recite it.
Then he spoke the Great Vidyārāja Uṣṇīṣavijayā:
*Tadyathā | dhara dhara dhara dhara dhara dhara dhara dhara*.
Dhāri dhāri dhāri dhāri dhāri dhāri dhāri dhāru dhāru dhāru dhāru dhāru dhāru dhāru dhāru sūru sūru sūru sūru sūru sūru sūru.
Mara mara mara mara mara mara mara mara mili mili mili mili mili mili mili mili mulu mulu mulu mulu mulu mulu mulu mulu.
Protect me and all sentient beings:
hīle hīle hīle hīle hīle hīle hīle hīle hīle | huru huru huru huru huru huru huru huru huru |
Kiri kiri kiri kiri kiri kiri kiri kiri kiri mili mili mili mili mili mili mili mili mili mili jili jili jili jili jili jili jili jili jili.
Zuru zuru zuru zuru zuru zuru zuru zuru zuru zuru sarva-bhūta-pratiṣṭhaṃ kārūṇi svāhā.
All enemies who harbor malicious intent and those who inflict extreme harm.

If one wishes to perform various evil deeds against myself and other sentient beings to cause them to fall ill, or desires to obstruct and block them so that they cannot see with their eyes or hear with their ears.
The nose cannot discern scents and the mouth cannot speak;
even as every part of their body desires to be bound,
those enemies— whether acting on their own or inciting others to do so— [inflict this].
Even those who follow and rejoice in such [practices] shall all be destroyed.
*Dhuru dhuru dhuru dhuru svāhā*. All *kiṃnaras*, *piśācas*, *vetālas*, and whirlwind spirits (*vātayakṣas*).
All such spirits and ghosts as these,
who might give rise to malicious intent or act to cause harm,
shall retreat and disperse in the four directions, departing far away.
Cala cala svāhā | Mara mara svāhā | Mili mili svāhā | Turu turu svāhā | May all humans and non-humans who give rise to evil intentions [be subdued].
It restrains both myself and other sentient beings,
causing them to become deranged or as if deluded;
it completely dispels all that has been done or is intended to be done.

Nṛte nṛgate svāhā | Vidyate vidyate svāhā | Rukṣite rukṣite svāhā | Avadate avadate svāhā | Śvete śvetavāsas-taradhāraṇīye svāhā | [This is] for protection against fear of kings, fear of thieves, fear of water, fire, and so forth.
Fear of nāginīs, fear of piśācas,
fear of kumbhāṇḍas, fear of kaṭapūtanas,
fear of shadows, and fear of all such evil spirits and ghosts— whether on the road or in the wilderness.
Whether traveling by day or night, they shall be entirely secure and at ease.
Furthermore, upon seeing their enemies, those enmities shall be resolved; upon hearing their words, those hostilities shall be dissolved.
They shall rejoice upon meeting one another, just like close kinsmen.
Tadyathā: hulu hulu, niji niji, rini rini, svāhā! May all malevolent mantras be cut off and destroyed!
Some are self-immolated until they are like ashes;
some harm themselves, or become deluded and distracted;
some are pinned by stakes and collapse, or vanish and disappear from sight.
Alternatively, rites performed based on emptiness may naturally fall away;
or there may be obstacles caused by written characters that prevent their efficacy.
Then the realm of King Yama trembles with fear and alarm.
Tadyathā | ṣṭha ṣṭha | ṭha ṭha ṭha ṭha ṭha ṭha | bhu ru bhu ru | mu ru mu ru svāhā | If Māra or a Māra-minion should direct an evil mind toward one another...
Whether they be Maheśvara, yakṣas, yakṣiṇīs, and so forth,
up to all those who feed on blood,
those who feed on flesh, and those who feed on fat and grease.
Those who consume vital essence, those who consume saliva and froth—
all such beings bound and fettered by these [conditions] are completely liberated,
even including men and women undergoing conception and dwelling within the womb.
At the time of their first birth, all shall attain peace and security.
Ānanda, this most venerable and supreme Great Wisdom Queen is the mother of the world;
all sentient beings are her children.
Ānanda, if any son or daughter of good family should hear such a supreme and exalted vidyā-mantra and be able to receive,
uphold, read, and recite it.
All sinful karma accumulated by this person since beginningless time shall be completely extinguished;
all forms of auspiciousness shall increase,
those who see them shall rejoice, and whatever they undertake shall be accomplished.
Furthermore, if good sons or good daughters write this vidyārāja on paper or cloth and constantly wear it upon their heads or arms;
All inauspicious things will be entirely removed;
even in dreams, there shall be no evil visions.
Fire cannot burn them, and water cannot sweep them away.
All evils shall not inflict harm.
Furthermore, one may scoop up water, recite this Vidyārāja over it,
and after consecrating it, inhale it through the nostrils.
All karmic residues from past lives within one's body shall also be extinguished;
furthermore, skillfulness shall increase and one will constantly attain peace and happiness.
All malevolent spells, incantations, and harmful deeds shall be neutralized.
With this, using consecrated water, thread, or white mustard seeds empowered by the vidyārāja,
one may dispel [obstacles] and withdraw oneself.
Ānanda, I have previously told you this.
This Great Vidyārāja was proclaimed together by seven koṭis of Tathāgatas in the past;
I now proclaim it again for the sake of future sentient beings who lack merit and virtue.
There are various malevolent spirits who cause all manner of disturbances, preventing one from attaining peace and stability.
Therefore, I proclaim this for you to receive and uphold well, so that it may be transmitted without interruption into the future.
He shall act as a source of reliance for all sentient beings.
At that time, having spoken this Sovereign Great Vidyārāja,
the World-Honored One, the Venerable Ānanda rejoiced, accepted it with faith, prostrated before the Buddha, and withdrew.
The Sūtra on the Great Vidyārāja Uṣṇīṣavijayā Spoken by the Buddha.
